person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually verified NARA row supplies Paul A. Borel and Box 69. An official CIA biographical record expands the name to Paul Arnold Borel, and a 1983 professional-fraternity profile documents the same engineering, WWII, and 1947-1972 CIA career sequence. The uncommon name and institutional continuity make the match high confidence, while the Box 69 file remains the direct confirmation route.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 69 and Borel's personnel chronology to order Sun Oil, Black and Veatch, and Phillips Petroleum, identify the final civilian employer, and establish his military-government/civil-affairs transition into OSS.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually verified index supplies only Frances Borger and Box 69, without a middle name, rank, service identifier, note, or location clue beyond the repository shelf location. Exact-name OSS, CIA, Army, occupation, employer, obituary, newspaper, institutional, and archival searches did not produce a source that identifies the indexed person. A family-history bank-clerk phrase is syntactically ambiguous, unsourced, and not accepted.
person_updates.next_action: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed. Review Box 69 for Frances Borger's full name, personnel status, hometown, occupation, employer, and OSS appointment chronology.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index identifies William H. Borger as civilian personnel and supplies no private identifier. The Army merged file contains an exact-name private candidate entering as an Army private in July 1944, but the name is not unique, the index status differs, and no independent OSS, hometown, occupation, or employer evidence connects that Army row to Box 69. A World War I Navy namesake and much later Navy officer are rejected.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 69 for William H. Borger's birth data, wartime status, employer, and any Army identifier before accepting or rejecting the 1944 exact-name Army candidate. No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually verified index and official Army merged file share the rare Lawrence Borgerding name; the index identifier carries an RA prefix and is one digit shorter than the Army row for Lawrence H. J. Borgerding. A 2025 obituary identifies Lawrence Hugo Borgerding, reports 1945 high-school graduation, a subsequent Army draft, Germany service, and OSS work. Identity is high confidence, but the official December 1945 Army-entry date conflicts with the obituary's wartime OSS chronology.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 69 and original Army records to resolve the one-digit identifier difference and the conflict between a December 1945 Army-entry date and reported wartime OSS service. Determine whether the record reflects OSS, SSU, or another assignment.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually verified index identifies First Lieutenant John M. Borgerson in Box 69. A 1988 scholarly periodical article, using biographical information from Borgerson's widow, identifies John M. Borgerson as a former OSS man assigned to Detachment 101 in August 1944 and later refers to him as Colonel. The uncommon exact name, explicit OSS linkage, and compatible rank progression support high confidence; the private identifier remains uncorroborated.
person_updates.next_action: No reliable pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed. Review Box 69 for Borgerson's pre-OSS Army unit, civilian occupation or employer, commissioning history, and August 1944 transfer into Detachment 101.

person_updates.next_action: The official Army-entry record supplies only a broad skilled miscellaneous-products manufacturing category. Review Box 69 for the exact trade, named employer, dates, Army unit, and Army-to-OSS sequence.
